A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GATEAU research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations, human evaluation, and an out-of-distribution case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds ChatGLM experiments, further ablations, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The main HMG, CAM, weighted selection score, and training objective remain unchanged. Appendices I.3–I.4 introduce exploratory variants using cluster-based selection and in-context alignment before HMG scoring. Procedural changes are limited to these supplementary variants.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongAlign and ShareGPT, the same LongBench datasets, LongBench-Chat, MT-Bench, needle retrieval, and the debate-summary case study. ChatGLM adds a model configuration within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal comparators remain Perplexity Guidance, CaR, Cherry Selection, and the existing training controls. v2 adds HMG-only and CAM-only comparisons for 13B models in Table 3, plus diversity-preserving and ICL-aligned variants in Tables 10 and 12.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets, data mixtures, selection percentages, and evaluation metrics are retained. Added experiments introduce ChatGLM3-6B configurations, segment lengths from 64 to 2048, clustering controls, and three-example ICL scoring. Appendix I.3 states 4300 + 70 samples despite describing a 50% comparison, leaving that control's exact sample budget unclear.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence with 13B component ablations, segment-length sensitivity, runtime comparisons, diversity-preserving selection, base-model perplexity measurements, and ICL alignment tests. The earlier alpha sweep, normalization and non-homologous-model analyses, needle test, human evaluation, and OOD case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging two GPT-4 evaluations. Neither provides training-seed variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched existing benchmark and HMG-analysis values remain unchanged apart from equivalent rounding. Substantial new results include ChatGLM comparisons, 13B ablations, sensitivity and runtime results, and mixed effects from diversity and ICL variants. For example, v2 Table 7 newly reports real-world ChatGLM LongBench-Chat scores of 60.2 with selection versus 55.9 with full-data training.

T1.justification: The substantive definitions and equations (1)–(7) are retained. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs; the added arguments concern empirical interpretation and experimental configurations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: selecting samples rich in long-range dependencies through HMG and CAM improves alignment, including outperforming full-data training using a small selected subset. The shortened wording preserves this claim.

C2.justification: New Section 6 identifies dependence on available homologous checkpoints and unsuitability for improving a targeted capability such as mathematics. Appendix I adds substantial interpretations concerning execution costs, memory requirements, transfer to other model families, implicit sample diversity, and the usefulness of base-model perplexity.

D1.justification: v2 adds a planned code, data, and model release location, runtime measurements, caching and parallel-execution details, and implementation information for clustering and ICL variants. Existing training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are retained. Some details are omitted, including the CaR reward model's previously stated 355M parameter count.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lin et al. on URIAL and Zeng et al. on GLM-130B, while removing the Giraffe and LM-Infinite references. The main positioning against short-instruction data-selection methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title and abstract, edits the introduction extensively, moves Related Work after the experiments, and relocates training explanations into the appendix. The appendices are reorganized from A–D into A–I with a roadmap and separate analysis sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from primarily single-column to two-column layout. LongBench tables are regrouped by evaluation metric, LongBench-Chat and MT-Bench tables are merged, and the needle figure moves to the appendix. Existing prompts and the case study become numbered figures; new tables and a segment-length plot are added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's already extensive evaluation, v2 provides useful additional validation through ChatGLM experiments, 13B ablations, sensitivity tests, cost reporting, and explicit limitations. These strengthen practical assessment while retaining the original evidence. The gains are tempered by the diversity experiment's inconsistent sample budget and its strong diversity interpretation from mixed downstream results.
